pr_title: feat(ivy): integrate indexing pipeline with NgtscProgram
pr_body:
Add an IndexingContext class to store indexing information and a
transformer module to generate indexing analysis. Integrate the indexing
module with the rest of NgtscProgram and add integration tests.

Closes #30959

issue_context.title: Component Analysis API for `NgtscProgram`
issue_context.body:
# Component Analysis API for `NgtscProgram`

### Relevant Package
This feature request is for @angular/compiler-cli.

### Description
This issue proposes exposing a new API on `NgtscProgram` that produces semantic information about components discovered in the program for use by an Angular indexer.

[Design Document](https://hackmd.io/@X3ECPVy-RCuVfba-pnvIpw/BkDUxaW84/%2FwqhNytHfR--9h4OVdox87g?type=book) on Ivy Design Docs

### Describe the solution you'd like
An API on `NgtscProgram` that generates semantic information about components, using the Ivy compilation pipeline (specifically `IvyCompilation` and `DecoratorHandler`s). Generation of semantic information will be housed in a new package `ngtsc/indexer`. More details on the [design document](https://hackmd.io/@X3ECPVy-RCuVfba-pnvIpw/BkDUxaW84/%2FwqhNytHfR--9h4OVdox87g?type=book).

### Describe alternatives you've considered
- Previously, extraction of semantic information about components was done via reliance on internal compiler APIs and unwrapping of private fields, which is not maintainable.
- Another alternative is to expose fields on the Program and Compilation, but this is also undesirable as it eliminates opaqueness of the compiler.

review_comments:
I think there's a bug in `ExpressionVisitor` (maybe not in this method). Consider the template:

```html
<input ngModel #model="ngModel">
{{model.valid}}
```

Here the `#model` reference defines a reference to the `NgModel` directive on the `<input>`, _not_ a property of the component itself. So the expression `{{model.valid}}` will generate an AST of `PropertyRead(PropertyRead(ImplicitReceiver, 'model'), 'valid')`. This will look to the `ExpressionVisitor` currently like `model` is a property of the component, since it will hone in on the `PropertyRead(ImplicitReceiver)` and add this as an `IdentifierKind.Property` identifier. Really it's not, it's a different kind of identifier entirely.

Another example:

```html
<user-view *ngFor="let user of users" [data]="user"></user-view>
```

Here in `[data]="user"`, the `user` expression (`PropertyRead(ImplicitReceiver, 'user')`) is a variable of the child template created by `*ngFor` and also not a property on the component instance.

The trick here is to use the `BoundTarget.getExpressionTarget` method to check if the `PropertyRead` `AST` has a target within the template. It'll return `null` if the expression is pointing at the component itself.

Does that make sense?

Yeah, that makes sense. I’ll implement the BoundTarget trick; thanks for that tip!

Bugs like this are also fairly benign, though, in terms of their effect on indexing a source code. Working with a language analysis tool like Kythe, I’ve learned that the typical philosophy is to worry more about not crashing the the indexer than emitting correct entries. That is, we should totally strive to extract identifiers correctly, but pointing references to something that doesn’t actually exist or is the incorrect reference is not catastrophic, it’s just best-effort. Especially since the TypeScript code identifiers are not indexed, some references can _only_ be best-effort.
Add a comment explaining _why_ re-parsing the template is necessary.

Add a comment here describing why we extract this to a function (so the indexer can re-parse the template later if needed). It should mention that re-parsing isn't always possible (e.g. it's not if the template was parsed in pre-analysis), but that's okay because indexing and pre-analysis don't run together ever.
I thought I had this but I guess not. Moved the second half of the suggested comment to where `parseTemplate` is instantiated inside the preanalyze block.
Generally for readability, there should be an empty line between the docstring and the jsdoc comments. Can you add this throughout?
When/why would this be `null`?  If it's possible, add it to the doc string.
